name: Adi Jagannatha Perumal Temple, Thiruppullani
deity: Vishnu as Adi Jagannatha Perumal, with the Goddess Padmasini Thayar — and Rama as Darbhasayana Rama, reclining on a bed of darbha grass
period: A Divya Desam of the Pandya country near the sea at Ramanathapuram, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Pandya, with Chola and Sethupathi patronage
summary: Near the sea at Ramanathapuram, Vishnu stands as Adi Jagannatha Perumal and Rama lies on his bed of darbha grass, awaiting the ocean — a Divya Desam of the Pandya country sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Thiruppullani lies near the coast just outside Ramanathapuram, on the road of the Rama legend that runs to Sethu and Rameswaram. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Pandya Nadu, glorified by Thirumangai Alvar in twenty verses of his Periya Thirumozhi. Tradition places the temple's beginnings in the eighth century, and the shrine grew with gifts from the Medieval Cholas, the later Pandyas and the Sethupathi rulers of Ramnad, the hereditary guardians of the causeway country. A damaged inscription of the thirty-seventh year of Maravarman Sundara Pandya records an order of a minister named Arya Chakravarthy, and historians suggest that parts of the gopuram may owe something to the Jaffna kings who held Rameswaram as allies of the Pandyas.
sections.architecture: The temple holds three great presences under their own vimanas. Adi Jagannatha Perumal, honoured as the Jagannatha of the south, stands beneath the Kalyana vimana with the Goddess Padmasini Thayar in her separate shrine. Darbhasayana Rama reclines on his grass bed under the Swastika vimana, and Pattabhi Rama, crowned after the victory, has his own sannidhi. Before the temple lies the Chakra Theertham, named for the Lord's discus, while the sea nearby is honoured as the Ratnakara theertham.
sections.legends: The name is read as Thiru-pul-anai, the sacred bed of grass. The sthala purana tells that the sages Pullar, Galavar and Kanvar did penance in a forest of darbha here, and Vishnu appeared to them first as a sacred fig and then as Adi Jagannatha. In the Ramayana tradition, Rama lay on darbha grass at this shore for three days, beseeching the sea-king for passage to Lanka; when the ocean gave no answer he took up his bow, and the sea-king came to him in surrender. Tradition also holds that King Dasaratha prayed here for sons.
sections.festivals: The Brahmotsavam is celebrated in the Tamil month of Panguni, and the birth festival of Rama in Chithirai draws pilgrims on the Rameswaram route. Vaikunta Ekadashi and the processions of Darbhasayana Rama and Adi Jagannatha keep the year; confirm festival dates locally.
sections.experience: Many pilgrims to Rameswaram stop here first, to stand before the Rama who lay waiting on the shore before the bridge was built. The darbha-bed form, the crowned Rama and the Lord of the south together make this a Divya Desam where the Ramayana feels close at hand.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Panguni Brahmotsavam, the Rama festival and Vaikunta Ekadashi are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruppullani is about 10 km from Ramanathapuram town, reached by road; Ramanathapuram has a railway station on the Madurai–Rameswaram line, and the nearest airport is Madurai. Pilgrims often visit on the way to Sethukarai and Rameswaram.
